column2: Welcome to the Dari course format. A two-minute look at what Dari adds to this course. Leave whenever you like.
The banner. It holds the course name, progress and quick actions. Upload your own image in course settings, or generate one.
Make a banner. Creates a banner image from the course name in the background, using your site's AI provider. Keep working while it runs.
Completion ring. It counts only activities with completion tracking turned on. If it looks low, check which activities track completion.
Course map. You can show the course map separately on the course page, on section pages and on activity pages (course settings).
Sections as blocks. Each section is a block showing its activities and learner progress. Give each an icon and choose a grid or list layout in course settings.
Choosing icons. While editing, select a section's icon to change it. Sections without one show a plain placeholder.
Time estimates. Each activity has an estimated time, and section totals add them up. Defaults are in the site settings; quiz times are worked out from their questions.
Activity lists. Each block lists its activities and marks the finished ones. Limit the list or turn it off in course settings.
Player panel. When it is turned on, the course map becomes a player panel: logo, course, progress ring, total time, and one row per activity with its time and a tick.
Gradebook shortcut. Goes straight to the gradebook. Learners see the same button, but only their own grades.
Ask Dari. Learners ask questions here. It reads this course's content, so its answers are about your material.
Preview as a learner. Learners see a simpler page: the Course, Settings and Participants tabs and all editing controls are hidden by default.
Tutor insights. The course menu has a report on how learners use the tutor: what they ask, where they get stuck, and which activities raise the most questions.
Where the settings are. Everything in this tour is configurable per course under Settings, and site-wide under Plugins, Course formats, Dari course format.
End of tour. Restart it any time from your preferences. Try the learner view next.
Let's get you started. A one-minute look at how this course works. Skip it whenever you like.
Progress so far. The ring and bar show how much of the course you have completed, and they update as you go.
Your completion. The ring counts only the activities your teacher tracks, so it may not include everything you can see.
The course map. Every section and activity is listed here. Pick any of them to go straight there.
Sections. Each block is one section of the course. It shows what is inside and how much of it you have done.
Time to allow. Every activity shows an estimated time, and each section adds them up. Use it to plan your study time.
Done and still to do. A filled square means finished; an empty one is still waiting. Some activities finish themselves; others you mark yourself.
Everything in one panel. This panel lists the whole course. Each row shows about how long it takes, and gets a tick when you finish. The ring at the top shows your overall progress.
Your marks. Opens your grades for this course. Only you can see them.
Your Ask Dari. Stuck? Ask the tutor. It knows this course and helps you work things out instead of just giving you the answer.
All set. Choose a section to begin.
